## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A blinded comparison of three independent laboratories using PPMI CSF samples reported sensitivities of 86–96% and specificities of 93–100%, demonstrating reproducibility in expert laboratories despite methodological differences. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8572469/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The 2025 biomatrix meta-analysis reported pooled blood SAA sensitivity of 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.93) and specificity of 0.91 (0.86–0.95); these pooled estimates are limited by aggregate data, publication bias and heterogeneous studies, and do not establish a universal blood-test performance. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12192484/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] In an analysis of PPMI and Tübingen cohort data, baseline SAA time-to-threshold predicted cognitive decline in both PPMI (hazard ratio 2·36, 95% CI 1·60–3·46) and Tübingen (2·17, 1·07–4·41), and was associated with cognitive decline in an Alzheimer-biomarker-negative PPMI subgroup. This was an observational prognostic association. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40541208/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] NfL interpretation needs covariate adjustment: the head-to-head study found associations with age in both CSF and plasma, and with body mass index, estimated glomerular filtration rate and chronic kidney disease in plasma. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12037818/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The FDA’s August 19, 2024 Letter of Support recommends CSF SAA as a susceptibility/risk biomarker for trial enrichment and supports binary SAA assessment for selection into trials targeting common synuclein biology; its stated context is drug development and clinical trials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-08-19) — https://www.fda.gov/media/181368/download · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] A Viewpoint cautions against premature adoption of the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay as a Parkinson disease biomarker test in general neurology practice; this is an attributed clinical-implementation caution. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39102226/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] Neurofilament light chain can be measured in CSF and plasma as a marker of axonal damage; higher levels have been associated with poorer cognitive outcomes in Parkinson disease, but it is nonspecific and also rises with age and other inflammatory or degenerative conditions. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 2023 cross-sectional PPMI study, CSF SAA sensitivity for clinically diagnosed Parkinson disease was 87·7% (95% CI 84·9–90·5) and specificity against healthy controls was 96·3% (93·4–99·2); these estimates describe that study population rather than general-population screening. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10627170/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] SAA positivity is heterogeneous: in the 2023 PPMI study, sensitivity in sporadic Parkinson disease with olfactory deficit was 98·6%, compared with 78·3% without olfactory deficit. A negative result therefore cannot universally exclude clinically diagnosed Parkinson disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10627170/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] NfL is a marker of neuroaxonal injury that can complement alpha-synuclein SAA, rather than directly measuring alpha-synuclein seeds. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12037818/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] In the 2025 head-to-head NfL study, CSF assays discriminated Parkinson’s disease from atypical parkinsonian disorders more accurately than plasma assays (AUC 0.966–0.974 versus 0.917–0.924); combining CSF NfL with alpha-synuclein RT-QuIC improved accuracy in that cohort. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12037818/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] The 2024 Zarkali review reports associations of baseline CSF Alzheimer-related biomarkers—higher phosphorylated tau, lower amyloid-beta 42, and lower amyloid-beta 42/total tau ratio—with worsening motor and cognitive performance at follow-up; these characterize co-pathology and prognosis rather than alpha-synuclein seeding itself. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] In a blinded 30-site cross-sectional study, skin biopsy detected cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein in 92.7% (89 of 96) of patients with PD, 98.2% (54 of 55) with MSA, 96.0% (48 of 50) with DLB and 100% (22 of 22) with pure autonomic failure, versus 3.3% (4 of 120) of controls; the authors state that further research in unselected clinical populations is needed to externally validate the findings. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10955354/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Alpha-synuclein SAA detects seeding-competent misfolded aggregates by amplifying their ability to template recombinant alpha-synuclein aggregation; thioflavin T fluorescence detects the resulting fibrils. RT-QuIC and PMCA are related SAA approaches. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8572469/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12192484/
- [statement] Expert-laboratory concordance does not remove the need for assay standardization: protocol heterogeneity, recombinant substrate, buffers, beads, shaking, temperature, and preanalytical handling affect comparability. (high confidence) — https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/acn3.70384 · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13347450/
- [statement] Blood alpha-synuclein assays require control of peripheral contamination and sample handling: erythrocytes and platelets contribute alpha-synuclein, and hemolysis and storage conditions can vary results. CSF SAA also requires preanalytical controls, including blood contamination and freeze-thaw handling. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12192484/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13347450/
- [statement] SAA seeding activity and total CSF alpha-synuclein concentration are different measurements: the 2024 Zarkali review found that total CSF alpha-synuclein did not show a consistent relationship with Lewy body pathology or longitudinal motor or cognitive change. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers
- [statement] Longitudinal prognostic results differ by analysis: a PPMI analysis found no statistically significant association between baseline seeding measures and progression among manifest patients, whereas a separate analysis associated baseline time-to-threshold with subsequent cognitive decline in PPMI and an independent Tübingen cohort. Diagnostic positivity should not be treated as an established general progression measure. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12354789/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40541208/
- [statement] CSF sampling is relatively invasive, motivating SAA studies in other specimens. The 2024 Zarkali review describes promising skin-biopsy results and lower accuracy with olfactory-mucosa sampling; performance should be interpreted for the specimen and assay actually tested. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11226684/ · keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

## Research summary — Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assays amplify seeding-competent aggregates and provide a molecular biomarker of synuclein pathology. CSF studies show strong diagnostic performance in selected cohorts, with clinically important heterogeneity in sensitivity. Cross-laboratory results are encouraging, but protocol and preanalytical standardization remain necessary. Diagnostic positivity is distinct from validated measurement of severity or progression. Blood assays offer less invasive sampling while introducing contamination and handling challenges. Neurofilament light chain measures neuroaxonal injury and can complement SAA, with interpretation influenced by biological covariates. FDA support described here concerns trial enrichment in its 2024 letter. Skin biopsy detection of phosphorylated alpha-synuclein is another tissue biomarker under evaluation.

## Source disagreement — Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

One PPMI analysis reported no significant baseline SAA–progression association among manifest patients; a separate analysis reported cognitive-decline associations for time-to-threshold in PPMI and Tübingen cohorts. The analyses differ in method and outcome, so they are not replications of the same endpoint.
